title: Scientists Are Teaching Birds to Sing Lost Songs
title_zh: 科学家正在教鸟类演唱失传的歌曲

paragraphs.en: This article was originally published by The Guardian and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration.
paragraphs.zh: 本文最初由《卫报》发表，此处作为 Climate Desk（气候台）合作内容的一部分予以转载。

paragraphs.en: A rufous-collared sparrow. Charles J. Sharp via Wikipedia
paragraphs.zh: 一只红领带鹀。Charles J. Sharp via Wikipedia

paragraphs.en: When bird populations decline, fledglings may struggle to learn the songs they need to attract mates. But new research suggests it is possible to teach birds lost songs.
paragraphs.zh: 当鸟类数量减少时，雏鸟可能难以学会吸引配偶所需的鸣叫声。 但新研究表明，教会鸟类失去的鸣叫声是有可能的。

sents.en: When bird populations decline, fledglings may struggle to learn the songs they need to attract mates.
sents.zh: 当鸟类数量减少时，雏鸟可能难以学会吸引配偶所需的鸣叫声。

sents.en: But new research suggests it is possible to teach birds lost songs.
sents.zh: 但新研究表明，教会鸟类失去的鸣叫声是有可能的。

paragraphs.en: Listening to birdsong is one of life’s great joys, but when researchers heard a particular tune emerging from a tree in a Buenos Aires park, they were especially jubilant. This arrangement was among those chirped by the local rufous-collared sparrows in the 1960s, but had since disappeared from the area.
paragraphs.zh: 聆听鸟鸣是人生一大乐事，但当研究人员在布宜诺斯艾利斯一座公园的树上听到一段特别的曲调时，他们格外欣喜。 这种鸣唱方式曾在20世纪60年代被当地的红领带鹀（rufous-collared sparrow）吟唱，但此后已从该地区消失。

sents.en: Listening to birdsong is one of life’s great joys, but when researchers heard a particular tune emerging from a tree in a Buenos Aires park, they were especially jubilant.
sents.zh: 聆听鸟鸣是人生一大乐事，但当研究人员在布宜诺斯艾利斯一座公园的树上听到一段特别的曲调时，他们格外欣喜。

sents.en: This arrangement was among those chirped by the local rufous-collared sparrows in the 1960s, but had since disappeared from the area.
sents.zh: 这种鸣唱方式曾在20世纪60年代被当地的红领带鹀（rufous-collared sparrow）吟唱，但此后已从该地区消失。

paragraphs.en: That was until scientists created a computer-generated rendition, curious to find out if birds might consider it realistic enough to imitate. Less than three months later, a local avian resident began to copy parts of the song.
paragraphs.zh: 直到科学家们创造出一种由计算机生成的版本，他们好奇鸟类是否会认为它足够逼真并加以模仿。 不到三个月后，当地的一只鸟类居民开始模仿这首鸣唱的部分内容。

sents.en: That was until scientists created a computer-generated rendition, curious to find out if birds might consider it realistic enough to imitate.
sents.zh: 直到科学家们创造出一种由计算机生成的版本，他们好奇鸟类是否会认为它足够逼真并加以模仿。

sents.en: Less than three months later, a local avian resident began to copy parts of the song.
sents.zh: 不到三个月后，当地的一只鸟类居民开始模仿这首鸣唱的部分内容。

paragraphs.en: There is a growing recognition of birdsong’s importance to conservation, and of the need to better understand how birds learn to sing. If an individual sings well, and in a familiar “dialect,” they are better placed to find a mate, defend their territory, and ultimately survive.
paragraphs.zh: 人们日益认识到鸟鸣对保护的重要性，也更加需要了解鸟类是如何学会鸣唱的。 如果一只鸟鸣唱得动听，并且带有熟悉的“方言”，它就更有可能找到配偶、保卫领地，并最终存活下来。

sents.en: There is a growing recognition of birdsong’s importance to conservation, and of the need to better understand how birds learn to sing.
sents.zh: 人们日益认识到鸟鸣对保护的重要性，也更加需要了解鸟类是如何学会鸣唱的。

sents.en: If an individual sings well, and in a familiar “dialect,” they are better placed to find a mate, defend their territory, and ultimately survive.
sents.zh: 如果一只鸟鸣唱得动听，并且带有熟悉的“方言”，它就更有可能找到配偶、保卫领地，并最终存活下来。

paragraphs.en: If a species’ population declines, however, there are fewer opportunities for fledglings to become good singers. Birds can begin to tweet abnormally or mistakenly learn the songs of other species , jeopardizing their chances of breeding.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，如果一个物种的种群数量下降，雏鸟成长为优秀“歌手”的机会就会减少。 鸟类可能会开始异常鸣叫，或错误地学会其他物种的鸣声，从而危及它们的繁殖机会。

sents.en: If a species’ population declines, however, there are fewer opportunities for fledglings to become good singers.
sents.zh: 然而，如果一个物种的种群数量下降，雏鸟成长为优秀“歌手”的机会就会减少。

sents.en: Birds can begin to tweet abnormally or mistakenly learn the songs of other species , jeopardizing their chances of breeding.
sents.zh: 鸟类可能会开始异常鸣叫，或错误地学会其他物种的鸣声，从而危及它们的繁殖机会。

paragraphs.en: Male birds are in a better position to attract a mate if they can sing well — which, broadly speaking, means their song is complex, sung consistently, and well performed. “If your song requires a lot of energy, you might have to be in quite a good condition to sing it,” says Rebecca Lewis, a conservation scientist at Chester Zoo.
paragraphs.zh: 雄鸟如果能唱好歌——大致来说，就是歌声复杂、唱得稳定、表现精湛——就更有可能吸引配偶。“如果你的歌声需要消耗大量能量，那你的身体必须处于相当好的状态才能唱出来，”切斯特动物园的保护科学家丽贝卡·刘易斯说。

paragraphs.en: “When people talk about biodiversity, we’re always talking about genes, about genetic material,” says Gabriel B. Mindlin, professor of physics at the University of Buenos Aires, who coauthored the study on rufous-collared sparrows, and whose work is featured in a Guardian-produced documentary, Dream of Birds .
paragraphs.zh: “当人们谈论生物多样性时，我们说的始终是基因，是遗传物质，”布宜诺斯艾利斯大学的物理学教授加布里埃尔·B. 明德林说，他是这项关于领歌雀研究的共同作者，其工作成果出现在一部由《卫报》制作的纪录片《鸟之梦》中。

sents.en: “When people talk about biodiversity, we’re always talking about genes, about genetic material,” says Gabriel B.
sents.zh: “当人们谈论生物多样性时，我们说的始终是基因，是遗传物质，”布宜诺斯艾利斯大学的物理学教授加布里埃尔·B.

sents.en: Mindlin, professor of physics at the University of Buenos Aires, who coauthored the study on rufous-collared sparrows, and whose work is featured in a Guardian-produced documentary, Dream of Birds .
sents.zh: 明德林说，他是这项关于领歌雀研究的共同作者，其工作成果出现在一部由《卫报》制作的纪录片《鸟之梦》中。

paragraphs.en: But animals’ learned behavior or culture, such as birdsong, is also an essential part of their population, says Mindlin.
paragraphs.zh: Mindlin 表示，但动物的习得行为或文化，例如鸟鸣，同样是其种群的重要组成部分。

paragraphs.en: The rufous-collared sparrow is not considered vulnerable globally, but researchers hope that synthetic recordings could help teach birdsong to other species whose populations are dwindling, allowing conservationists to tutor individuals where real-life recordings do not exist.
paragraphs.zh: 红领带鹀在全球范围内并不被认为是易危物种，但研究人员希望合成录音能够帮助向其他种群数量不断减少的物种教授鸟鸣，使自然保护主义者能够在没有真实录音的情况下对个体进行鸣声训练。

paragraphs.en: About 4,000 of the world’s 10,000 bird species are songbirds (or oscine passerines), such as finches, sparrows, and blackbirds, which generally have complex songs that are at least partly learned from other individuals. Their songs are hugely diverse, though separate research on the wider passerine group of birds, which incorporates songbirds, has identified common “motifs” or building blocks: three types of trill, three types of whistle, chaotic notes, and harmonic notes.
paragraphs.zh: 全世界一万种鸟类中约有四千种是鸣禽（即鸣禽类雀形目鸟），例如雀、麻雀和黑鹂，它们通常拥有复杂的鸣声，这些鸣声至少部分是从其他个体那里学来的。 它们的鸣声极其多样，不过，针对包含鸣禽在内的更广泛的雀形目鸟类的独立研究已经识别出常见的“母题”或基本构件：三种颤音、三种哨音、无序音符和谐波音符。

sents.en: About 4,000 of the world’s 10,000 bird species are songbirds (or oscine passerines), such as finches, sparrows, and blackbirds, which generally have complex songs that are at least partly learned from other individuals.
sents.zh: 全世界一万种鸟类中约有四千种是鸣禽（即鸣禽类雀形目鸟），例如雀、麻雀和黑鹂，它们通常拥有复杂的鸣声，这些鸣声至少部分是从其他个体那里学来的。

sents.en: Their songs are hugely diverse, though separate research on the wider passerine group of birds, which incorporates songbirds, has identified common “motifs” or building blocks: three types of trill, three types of whistle, chaotic notes, and harmonic notes.
sents.zh: 它们的鸣声极其多样，不过，针对包含鸣禽在内的更广泛的雀形目鸟类的独立研究已经识别出常见的“母题”或基本构件：三种颤音、三种哨音、无序音符和谐波音符。

paragraphs.en: The way that birds use these motifs reflects the environment in which the birds evolved. Flat whistles are more likely to be sung by birds in tropical rainforests where sound must travel through dense vegetation. Complex motifs, such as ultrafast trills, are more common in temperate regions where birds tend to communicate at closer range.
paragraphs.zh: 鸟类使用这些音型的方式反映了它们演化时所处的环境。 平直的哨音更常见于热带雨林中的鸟类，因为声音必须穿过茂密的植被传播。 复杂的音型，例如超快颤音，在温带地区更为常见，那里的鸟类往往在较近距离进行交流。

sents.en: The way that birds use these motifs reflects the environment in which the birds evolved.
sents.zh: 鸟类使用这些音型的方式反映了它们演化时所处的环境。

sents.en: Flat whistles are more likely to be sung by birds in tropical rainforests where sound must travel through dense vegetation.
sents.zh: 平直的哨音更常见于热带雨林中的鸟类，因为声音必须穿过茂密的植被传播。

sents.en: Complex motifs, such as ultrafast trills, are more common in temperate regions where birds tend to communicate at closer range.
sents.zh: 复杂的音型，例如超快颤音，在温带地区更为常见，那里的鸟类往往在较近距离进行交流。

paragraphs.en: The song studied by Mindlin was recreated based on hand-drawn annotations of rufous-collared sparrow songs that were made in the 1960s. Each song consists of a trill, which is consistent among individuals in the same region, and a theme, which varies. Some of the themes recorded decades ago are still sung by the local birds, but others have died out.
paragraphs.zh: Mindlin所研究的歌曲是根据20世纪60年代对领歌雀歌声的手绘标注 recreated（重现）的。 每首歌都由一个颤音和一个主题组成，颤音在同一地区的个体之间保持一致，而主题则各不相同。 几十年前记录的一些主题至今仍被当地的鸟儿传唱，但另一些已经消失了。

sents.en: The song studied by Mindlin was recreated based on hand-drawn annotations of rufous-collared sparrow songs that were made in the 1960s.
sents.zh: Mindlin所研究的歌曲是根据20世纪60年代对领歌雀歌声的手绘标注 recreated（重现）的。

sents.en: Each song consists of a trill, which is consistent among individuals in the same region, and a theme, which varies.
sents.zh: 每首歌都由一个颤音和一个主题组成，颤音在同一地区的个体之间保持一致，而主题则各不相同。

sents.en: Some of the themes recorded decades ago are still sung by the local birds, but others have died out.
sents.zh: 几十年前记录的一些主题至今仍被当地的鸟儿传唱，但另一些已经消失了。

paragraphs.en: It is not clear why the song studied by Mindlin had disappeared, though he notes the population of birds in the park had declined.
paragraphs.zh: 目前尚不清楚 Mindlin 所研究的歌曲为何消失了，不过他指出公园里的鸟类数量已经减少。

paragraphs.en: Birds’ songs can change naturally over time — for example, birds might make errors when learning songs, which then can become imprinted in future renditions. Human encroachment and population declines can also cause dramatic changes.
paragraphs.zh: 鸟类的鸣叫声会随着时间自然变化——例如，鸟类在学习鸣叫时可能出错，而这些错误随后可能在未来的鸣叫版本中固化下来。 人类活动的侵占和种群数量的下降也会导致剧烈的变化。

sents.en: Birds’ songs can change naturally over time — for example, birds might make errors when learning songs, which then can become imprinted in future renditions.
sents.zh: 鸟类的鸣叫声会随着时间自然变化——例如，鸟类在学习鸣叫时可能出错，而这些错误随后可能在未来的鸣叫版本中固化下来。

sents.en: Human encroachment and population declines can also cause dramatic changes.
sents.zh: 人类活动的侵占和种群数量的下降也会导致剧烈的变化。

paragraphs.en: Songbirds learn from other members of their species — such as a father or neighbors — which results in local groups developing their own dialects. The window for learning varies from a few weeks to a lifetime. Some species also have an innate level of knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 鸣禽会向同类中的其他成员学习——例如父亲或邻居——这使得地方群体形成了自己的方言。 学习窗口从几周到终生不等。 有些物种还具备天生的知识水平。

sents.en: Songbirds learn from other members of their species — such as a father or neighbors — which results in local groups developing their own dialects.
sents.zh: 鸣禽会向同类中的其他成员学习——例如父亲或邻居——这使得地方群体形成了自己的方言。

sents.en: The window for learning varies from a few weeks to a lifetime.
sents.zh: 学习窗口从几周到终生不等。

sents.en: Some species also have an innate level of knowledge.
sents.zh: 有些物种还具备天生的知识水平。

paragraphs.en: “There’s such a diversity in songbirds in how they learn,” says Sarah Collins, associate professor of animal behavior at the University of Plymouth, who studied a group of cirl buntings that were translocated from Devon to Cornwall as part of a conservation project.
paragraphs.zh: “鸣禽在学习方式上存在如此多样的差异，”普利茅斯大学动物行为学副教授莎拉·柯林斯说，她研究了一群作为保护项目一部分而从德文郡迁移到康沃尔郡的圃鹀。

paragraphs.en: Initially, the birds produced abnormal songs that were squeaky and slow, and far less diverse than those of the source populations in Devon. “They didn’t have the richness of sound,” says Collins. Eight years later, however, their songs had returned to normal.
paragraphs.zh: 起初，这些鸟发出的鸣叫异常，既尖细又缓慢，远不如德文郡源种群的鸣叫那样多样。“它们的鸣声缺乏丰富性，”柯林斯说。 然而，八年后，它们的鸣叫已恢复正常。

sents.en: Initially, the birds produced abnormal songs that were squeaky and slow, and far less diverse than those of the source populations in Devon. “They didn’t have the richness of sound,” says Collins.
sents.zh: 起初，这些鸟发出的鸣叫异常，既尖细又缓慢，远不如德文郡源种群的鸣叫那样多样。“它们的鸣声缺乏丰富性，”柯林斯说。

sents.en: Eight years later, however, their songs had returned to normal.
sents.zh: 然而，八年后，它们的鸣叫已恢复正常。

paragraphs.en: A few of the chicks were played recordings of cirl sounds, though not all. The study suggests that recovery of song is possible, though it is unclear if other species would bounce back in the same way. Cirl buntings are born with knowledge of the elements that make up the “notes” used in their songs, says Collins. “What they learn is how to put those elements together,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: 有几只雏鸟听了圃鹀叫声的录音，但并非所有雏鸟都听了。 该研究表明，鸣声的恢复是可能的，不过尚不清楚其他物种是否能以同样的方式恢复。 柯林斯说，圃鹀天生就知道构成其鸣声所用“音符”的各个元素。“它们学习的是如何把这些元素组合在一起，”她说。

sents.en: A few of the chicks were played recordings of cirl sounds, though not all.
sents.zh: 有几只雏鸟听了圃鹀叫声的录音，但并非所有雏鸟都听了。

sents.en: The study suggests that recovery of song is possible, though it is unclear if other species would bounce back in the same way.
sents.zh: 该研究表明，鸣声的恢复是可能的，不过尚不清楚其他物种是否能以同样的方式恢复。

sents.en: Cirl buntings are born with knowledge of the elements that make up the “notes” used in their songs, says Collins. “What they learn is how to put those elements together,” she says.
sents.zh: 柯林斯说，圃鹀天生就知道构成其鸣声所用“音符”的各个元素。“它们学习的是如何把这些元素组合在一起，”她说。

paragraphs.en: Some songbird species have a similar genetic underpinning and so may also be able to recover their songs, but others do not. Either way, Collins recommends a tutor to help other birds that are being translocated.
paragraphs.zh: 一些鸣禽物种具有类似的遗传基础，因此可能也能够恢复它们的歌声，但其他物种则不具备。 无论如何，柯林斯建议为其他被迁移的鸟类安排一名“教师”来提供帮助。

sents.en: Some songbird species have a similar genetic underpinning and so may also be able to recover their songs, but others do not.
sents.zh: 一些鸣禽物种具有类似的遗传基础，因此可能也能够恢复它们的歌声，但其他物种则不具备。

sents.en: Either way, Collins recommends a tutor to help other birds that are being translocated.
sents.zh: 无论如何，柯林斯建议为其他被迁移的鸟类安排一名“教师”来提供帮助。

paragraphs.en: A separate study in Australia tracked regent honeyeaters that were bred in zoos to boost a critically endangered wild population that had fallen to about 250 individuals. Interacting with just two wild-born male “tutors” helped the zoo-bred birds to learn to sing the wild songs. Thereafter, zoo-bred males that had learned the traditional songs went on to tutor the next generation.
paragraphs.zh: 澳大利亚的一项单独研究追踪了在动物园繁育的王吸蜜鸟，其目的是帮助一个数量已降至约250只的极度濒危野生种群。 仅与两只野生出身的雄性“导师”互动，就帮助动物园繁育的鸟类学会了唱野外歌曲。 此后，学会了传统歌曲的动物园繁育雄鸟又继续担当下一代的导师。

sents.en: A separate study in Australia tracked regent honeyeaters that were bred in zoos to boost a critically endangered wild population that had fallen to about 250 individuals.
sents.zh: 澳大利亚的一项单独研究追踪了在动物园繁育的王吸蜜鸟，其目的是帮助一个数量已降至约250只的极度濒危野生种群。

sents.en: Interacting with just two wild-born male “tutors” helped the zoo-bred birds to learn to sing the wild songs.
sents.zh: 仅与两只野生出身的雄性“导师”互动，就帮助动物园繁育的鸟类学会了唱野外歌曲。

sents.en: Thereafter, zoo-bred males that had learned the traditional songs went on to tutor the next generation.
sents.zh: 此后，学会了传统歌曲的动物园繁育雄鸟又继续担当下一代的导师。

paragraphs.en: “Sometimes birds don’t learn very well from CDs or just playbacks. They need some sort of interaction,” says Collins.
paragraphs.zh: “有时候，鸟类通过CD或单纯的录音回放学习效果并不好。 它们需要某种形式的互动，”柯林斯说。

sents.en: “Sometimes birds don’t learn very well from CDs or just playbacks.
sents.zh: “有时候，鸟类通过CD或单纯的录音回放学习效果并不好。

sents.en: They need some sort of interaction,” says Collins.
sents.zh: 它们需要某种形式的互动，”柯林斯说。

paragraphs.en: Bringing wild birds into captivity to teach hand-reared chicks could cause huge distress and bring disease, however, risking the health of individuals from an already endangered population. It is possible that A.I. could help provide live tutoring in the future.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，将野生鸟类带入圈养环境来教人工抚养的雏鸟，可能会造成巨大的痛苦并带来疾病，从而危及这一本已濒危种群中个体的健康。 未来，人工智能（A.I.）有可能帮助提供实时辅导。

sents.en: Bringing wild birds into captivity to teach hand-reared chicks could cause huge distress and bring disease, however, risking the health of individuals from an already endangered population.
sents.zh: 然而，将野生鸟类带入圈养环境来教人工抚养的雏鸟，可能会造成巨大的痛苦并带来疾病，从而危及这一本已濒危种群中个体的健康。

sents.en: It is possible that A.I. could help provide live tutoring in the future.
sents.zh: 未来，人工智能（A.I.）有可能帮助提供实时辅导。

paragraphs.en: Dialect is also important. Past translocation projects have shown that birds are slower to match if they do not sing in the same dialect. “Birds with mismatched songs don’t pair quite as quickly or do quite as well once they’re paired,” adds Lewis. Familiarizing birds with songs of their destination can help to mitigate this.
paragraphs.zh: 方言也很重要。 以往的迁移项目表明，如果鸟类不唱相同的方言，它们配对的速度会更慢。“歌声不匹配的鸟类配对不那么快，配对后表现也不那么好，”刘易斯补充道。 让鸟类提前熟悉目的地的歌声有助于缓解这一问题。

paragraphs.en: A huge volume of birdsong is now being recorded and uploaded into databases, including by a growing number of hobbyists interested in birdwatching, says Mindlin. “One day we’ll be grateful to have all those records,” he says. “I don’t think we still have an idea that really we have to register dialects and communication systematically.”
paragraphs.zh: 明德林说，如今大量的鸟鸣正在被录制并上传到数据库中，其中包括越来越多对观鸟感兴趣的爱好者。“总有一天我们会庆幸拥有所有这些记录，”他说。“我认为我们还没有真正意识到，我们必须系统性地记录方言和交流。”

paragraphs.en: In Buenos Aires, the song from the 1960s can still be heard. “It’s still being sung by just a few individuals, pretty close to where we inserted it,” he says, though only time will tell how long it persists.
paragraphs.zh: 在布宜诺斯艾利斯，这首诞生于20世纪60年代的歌曲依然能被听到。“目前只有少数几个人还在传唱，而且就在我们插入它的地点附近，”他说，不过它能持续多久，只有时间才能证明。

paragraphs.en: For America’s Rarest Wildlife, Survival May Hinge on a Single Word
